title: Sir Alex Ferguson taken to hospital before Manchester United vs. Liverpool
content:
Sir Alex Ferguson was taken to hospital ahead of Manchester United’s fixture against Liverpool at Old Trafford on Sunday.

Ferguson, United’s most successful manager, was in the tunnel area ahead of the game before being taken to hospital as a precaution.

The club, although not commenting formally, has said it was not a medical emergency.

Ferguson, 84, was pictured with Dr Aseem Malhotra before Sunday’s match, with the cardiologist uploading a photo with the the 84-year-old to social media.

“A privilege, honour and dream come true to be invited to spend some quality time with Sir Alex Ferguson ahead of the game against Liverpool today at old Trafford,” Malhotra’s post on X read.

Ferguson, who retired as United manager in 2013, is a regular visitor to the Old Trafford directors’ box and had made the trip for the Liverpool fixture.

Even though he saw his paid ambassadorial role cut by Sir Jim Ratcliffe, the club’s minority shareholder, in 2024 as part of a cost-cutting exercise, he has continued to be a visible presence around United.

In May 2018, Ferguson had to undergo life-saving surgery after suffering a brain haemorrhage and spent a period of time in intensive care. There is nothing at this stage to suggest Sunday’s events were linked to this previous health issue.

Ferguson is widely considered to be one of the greatest managers of all time after winning 13 Premier League titles at United between 1993 and 2013. Manchester City’s Pep Guardiola is his closest rival with six top-flight titles.

Ferguson also won two Champions Leagues at United, including in 1998-99, where they also lifted the Premier League and FA Cup to complete a historic treble. City are the only other English club to have completed the feat, doing so in 2023.

Including the 1998-99 season, Ferguson’s near 27-year spell in charge of the club saw them win five FA Cups, four League Cup titles and the previous iteration of the FIFA Club World Cup.
